source: Owner notes in chat during grilling round 3 (verbatim).
raw:
If its just buying/selling then yes towns will eventually run out of money due to Tax for each sale.
But people in each town produce money by consuming goods those towns purchase/produce.

So a town that is self sufficient(not really possible) would only sell and not buy resources, meaning they would generate gold over time, but our Kingdom would get 0% tax

---

Player job is to ensure that towns trade between each other so the  Crown can produce gold since Gold is required to place new towns and buildings for those towns.
Only upgrading those buildings uses that specific Town money(+ they need to buy resources)

as well as for research
outcome: New gold enters the Kingdom only when residents use Goods (paid into their Town's Purse).
Towns pay the Tariff on trade; a Town that only sells pays none (round 3 asks to confirm the buyer pays).
The player's job: keep Towns trading so the Treasury fills; the Treasury pays for founding Towns, placing buildings and research (Royal Traders buy its Goods with Treasury gold).
A Town's Purse pays for upgrading its buildings and buying Goods (Town level-ups asked in round 3).
